title: It builds. But can you ship it?

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: Good news. It builds. I've named the zip final, final, really final.

turns.speaker: litai
turns.text: A bold naming convention. Which tests passed on the version inside?

turns.speaker: litai
turns.text: Let's give your users something stronger than reassurance.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: Fine. Where do I actually get Literate A I? Please don't say it's already installed.

turns.speaker: litai
turns.text: Fair. Start at github dot com, slash jordan hubbard, slash literate dash A I. It's public. We're using a checkout, not a mystery package name.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: All right. What do I need before I copy commands?

turns.speaker: litai
turns.text: On this Mac: Python three eleven or newer, Git, and Make. Then clone the repository, enter its directory, and run make install.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: Is that about to install every compiler humanity has regretted?

turns.speaker: litai
turns.text: No. It checks the selected prerequisites and asks before installing missing ones. Read the prompt. We are building software, not adopting a package manager.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: And after the installer says done?

turns.speaker: litai
turns.text: Use the path it reports, then run lit eye version and lit eye doctor. If the command isn't found, fix your PATH first.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: So installing the harness also signs me into my coding agent?

turns.speaker: litai
turns.text: Not yet. Choose a supported coding agent and sign in separately. Don't put credentials in the project. Or this recording.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: Then we get to write code?

turns.speaker: litai
turns.text: First, tell me what the product should do. Then we'll watch the agent write code, and make it prove the result.
